correctness.rationale: Prime valuations evolve exactly by adjacent absolute differences. For p>m at most one of n..n+m is divisible by p; a single spike of height e evolves by parity of Pascal binomial coefficients, giving exactly the P_m(n) valuation. For each small p<=m, put B=floor(log_p(m)). At most one initial valuation exceeds B, since a difference <p^(B+1) cannot connect two such multiples. The one-spike stability induction says if exceptional height e>2^(m+1)B, every intermediate entry is epsilon*e+b with epsilon evolving by XOR and bounded error b; choosing truncation H=2^(m+1)(B+1)+1 ensures that replacing e by H shifts the output by epsilon_(m,j)(e-H). The same shift occurs in sum of the odd-binomial indexed initial valuations. Thus the valuation difference E_(m,p) depends only on the truncated vector modulo p^H, and is periodic. Chinese remainder assembles positive periodic c_m; Lucas binomial parity yields degree 2^s2(m), and uniform residue class frequency gives the atomic limit. Independent 1980 exact Z-game cells (m=0..10,n=1..180), all p>m valuations and m=2,3 formulas passed. This is a full fixed-generation theorem, not an m-uniform claim.

value.rationale: The natural-integer seed is the canonical original arithmetic game, not an artificial slice. An all-generation-index-fixed exact quasipolynomial with binary-popcount degree, periodic small-prime correction and limiting atomic distribution supplies natural invariants and structure beyond sparse numerical tomographies. Effective periods make each row computably classifiable even though the least period remains open.

limitations: Fixed m with n varying; no uniform growth as m tends to infinity and no minimal-period classification.
